correctness.rationale: With h=1/t the chord gain is n times the centered ramp variance divided by d+h, using the mean-zero inverse of the path Laplacian. Summing the ramp and its squares, with left and right constant tails, gives C_n(d)−d^2(l−r)^2/(4n). In wrong parity the best imbalance is one; for d>=3 the mean of the two neighboring centered numerators exceeds this by (n−d)^2/(4n), and the denominators average exactly. At wrong-parity d=2 the d=3 neighbor wins both in bare numerator and in numerator divided by length, so it wins for all h>0. For the centered samples, the adjacent difference after positive cross multiplication is h(d−1)(n+1−d)−d(d−2)(4d−3n−4)/6. The derivative of the continuous interpolant has positive numerator up to 3n/4, then a strictly decreasing numerator with derivative (n/2−x)(x+h). Any equality at an adjacent pair therefore places the unique peak strictly between those two lengths and makes that tie global. Positive crossing criteria form a contiguous block from the top; at each crossing the next lower pair is still ordered toward the higher length, so the times are strictly ordered. The first possible crossing is n=9 and has t=7/4. Independent exact-rational checks sum electrical series/parallel resistances, separating path-tail segments from the two cycle arcs; they reproduced the optimal values and all minimizing endpoints at the checked parameters.
residual_risks: Finite replay uses n=4..18, three fixed positive conductances and all positive transition points within those orders. Infinite coverage follows from the strict parity and comparison arguments, not that replay.
